PullRequest.Title: extensions: keep update checks on polling cadence
PullRequest.Body:
Do not reschedule the full installed-extension update check when an extension's auto-update delay expires. Clarify that delay expiry makes an update eligible rather than guaranteeing its installation time.

Addresses #339362 by keeping the UTD check cadence regular, not rescheduling to align immediately when an extension exits quarantine.  

Prior to that PR, the maximum delay for an auto-update was max(Cadence).  With that change and the alignment of 12-hr quarantine and 12-hr cadence, the maximum became max(Quarantine) - which would always be less than 2*max(Cadence).  The changes in this PR can cause the maximum delay between publish and auto-update to increase to max(Quarantine+Cadence), which could be as much as double, but maintains both the quarantine and the distributed rollout.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each earliest quarantine expiry initiated another full installed-extension update check outside the normal cadence. For N installed extensions this repeated O(N) metadata and synchronization work and could launch N concurrent latest-version HTTP GETs, or a grouped marketplace query POST.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Quarantine expiry caused an additional marketplace update-check burst, increasing network traffic and CPU/serialization beyond the regular polling cadence.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Removing the expiry timer keeps full marketplace checks on the existing 12-hour scheduler, avoiding the extra full synchronization and network burst when an extension becomes eligible.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Deleted base line 2306 scheduled eventuallyCheckForUpdates(true) at the earliest delay expiry. That cancels the cadence delayer, immediately runs checkForUpdates(), builds infos for all installed extensions, and calls galleryService.getExtensions(infos). The resource API uses Promise.all over those infos and sends a GET per UUID-backed extension; its fallback sends a grouped query POST. The added fake-timer test counts getExtensions and proves that crossing expiry no longer adds a check, while the unchanged scheduler still checks every 12 hours.

Scenarios.Scenario: Automatic extension update polling when a newly published update is still inside the configured delay window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initialization at LifecyclePhase.Eventually schedules an immediate background check, then the unchanged ThrottledDelayer polls every 12 hours. Marketplace completion is required to discover updated metadata and then trigger auto-update, but it is off the interactive startup critical path. Before this PR, the earliest delay expiry also canceled the cadence timer and put the same full check on that background path immediately; the PR removes that extra path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch latest marketplace metadata for all installed eligible extensions; resource API sends concurrent per-extension GETs, while query API sends a grouped POST and can perform fallback requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to N concurrent GETs for N UUID-backed installed extensions on the resource API, or one grouped POST for the query API, with fallback calls for misses/errors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The regular 12-hour poll made this call, and delay expiry additionally invoked it immediately and reset the next poll. The diff removes the delay-expiry invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before refreshed gallery state can mark updates outdated and invoke auto-update; background rather than interactive startup-critical.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Hand eligible extension updates to extension-management servers, which download and install extension packages and mutate extension files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One install task per eligible outdated extension, launched together by Promises.settled; server routing/grouping occurs downstream.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same install path ran after the expiry-triggered refresh; the PR does not add calls and can defer them until the next cadence poll.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for automatic update completion, but remains background work and now begins after the next regular poll rather than at quarantine expiry.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The installed marketplace-extension set N. checkForUpdates constructs N extension infos. With the latest-version resource API, effective request cardinality is up to N UUID-backed extensions; with the query API it is one grouped POST, plus fallback requests for misses. Delayed extensions are coalesced to the single earliest expiry timer before the PR, not one timer per extension.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The regular update scheduler is globally serialized/coalesced by one ThrottledDelayer. Before the PR, one MutableDisposable held the earliest delay timer, whose immediate trigger canceled and reset that scheduler. Inside the resource API, UUID-backed extension requests use unbounded Promise.all across N; query-API work is grouped. This concurrency is pre-existing, and the PR removes one occasion on which it runs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The gallery manifest and common headers are reused, but the traced getExtensions paths issue fresh HTTP requests; no result cache or negative cache was found on this path. Warm process state therefore does not eliminate the quarantine-expiry request. The PR leaves normal cold/startup and 12-hour polls unchanged and removes only the expiry-triggered full refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the deleted timer directly invoked the immediate full check, the transitive HTTP requests are explicit, and the added fake-timer test proves the extra getExtensions call no longer occurs.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: User extension counts, gallery resource-API availability, fallback frequency, and request durations vary. The removed extra check and its N-scaling resource path are directly established despite uncertain aggregate traffic savings.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced regression. This is a concrete performance fix: it removes repeated collection-wide marketplace/network work while preserving the normal polling cadence. The fix was recorded with report_regression_fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Changing extensions.autoUpdate or extensions.autoUpdateDelay while outdated extensions are present
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The configuration listener synchronously tests affected keys and fires the change event; when auto-update is enabled it schedules autoUpdateExtensions through the existing 1-second ThrottledDelayer. Any installs must finish only for update completion, not for the settings write or UI response. The PR removes cancellation/rescheduling of the separate quarantine timer because that timer no longer exists.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potentially fetch a gallery manifest when consent metadata is absent, then download eligible updates through extension management.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one consent-manifest path and one install task per eligible outdated extension after the coalesced scan; zero for disabled or still-delayed updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same coalesced scan and install work occurred. The old listener additionally canceled or rescheduled the expiry timer; this diff removes that timer state without adding boundary calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the settings-change critical path because eventuallyAutoUpdateExtensions schedules the work; required only for update installation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The current outdated-extension set M is scanned once per coalesced configuration event. At most M eligible extensions proceed to consent checks and installs; repeated setting changes within the delayer window coalesce.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Configuration-triggered auto-update scans are coalesced by the single autoUpdateDelayer. Eligible installs use Promises.settled and may run concurrently per extension. The diff neither increases scan frequency nor install concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Eligibility uses already-held outdated/gallery metadata and the configured delay; no update-result cache is added or defeated. Consent may reuse gallery metadata or fetch a manifest only for the narrow code-introduction case. Removing the quarantine timer also removes its lifecycle/cancellation state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: listener, delayer, loop, and boundary paths are explicit and unchanged apart from timer removal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of outdated eligible extensions and manifest-cache state vary, but no changed mechanism increases work or concurrency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. Work remains coalesced and the PR reduces timer lifecycle work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering delayed auto-update status for an extension in the Extensions UI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action computes relative delay strings and constructs the same MarkdownString during status refresh. The only changed behavior is wording from guaranteed update time to eligibility time; no new render, layout, IPC, filesystem, database, subprocess, or network boundary is introduced.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One status calculation per rendered/refreshed extension action; the diff does not change collection cardinality or refresh frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous per-action string/Markdown construction, unchanged by the diff; no queue or boundary concurrency involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes. The same delay values and relative-time formatting are used before and after.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the hunk changes only localized text.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the changed string has equivalent construction cost.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and all diff pages. No diff-introduced performance findings were found. The main service change removes a proven repeated full marketplace update check at quarantine expiry; its introducing commit was identified and the regression fix recorded.
